BMGriffin_GRF6SDAG10.overview: Built in 2492 the Griffin was originally classified as a heavy BattleMech, filling in the weight gap between mammoth machines like the Mackie and smaller recon 'Mechs like the Wasp, and intended for close assaults
BMGriffin_GRF6SDAG10.capabilities: The massive and efficient fusion engine of the Griffin, giving it a cruising speed of 57.1 km/h, combined with five jump jets occupying the rear torso areas for a total jumping distance of 150 meters, is what distinguishes it from other medium 'Mechs and has kept the Griffin in the game over the centuries. Unfortunately, like most other early 'Mechs, the Griffin suffers from insufficient heat capacity with only twelve heat sinks installed. The result is that Griffin pilots, lacking the ability to do both, must choose at the outset of a fight whether to engage or withdraw. Nine and a half tons of armor plating compares quite favorably to many other medium 'Mechs, although as is often the case the Griffin will find itself in combat with larger 'Mechs. For this reason, two pairs of false armor baffles were added to the 'Mech, one on its shoulders providing limited protection to the LRM launcher and cockpit, and a smaller pair on the legs protecting the knees joints.

systems.label: Armor
systems.manufacturer: Starshield A Light Ferro-Fibrous armor with CASE

BMGriffin_GRF6SDAG10.history: Combining tremendous speed and firepower in one frame the Griffin briefly dominated in this role before being superseded by larger and better-equipped 'Mechs. However the Griffin was very popular among commanders and pilots alike and so Earthwerks Incorporated kept it in production, this time reclassified as a medium 'Mech and tasked with long-range fire support for medium lances. In this capacity the Griffin has excelled, combining good striking power, endurance and speed, with its only major weakness being a lack of close-range defensive weapons. During the Succession Wars the Griffin could be found in almost every unit of all the Great Houses, thanks in part to its diverse number of manufacturers. Besides being constructed from Earthwerks' factory on Keystone the Griffin was later acquired and built by Defiance Industries (Hesperus II), Kallon Industries (Talon), Brigadier Corporation (Oliver), and Norse BattleMech Works (later Victory Industries, Marduk). It was even manufactured in the Periphery by Vandenberg Mechanized Industries on Illiushin. Only the Capellan Confederation lacked a means of building the 'Mech, although they made up for it by purchasing a limited number from the Taurian Concordat. During the Fourth Succession War some of these manufacturers exchanged hands, with the Draconis Combine capturing Marduk from the Federated Suns and the Lyran Commonwealth taking Oliver from the Free Worlds League. This exchange also happened to coincide with several new variants being designed to exploit recently-recovered lostech. As such variants meant specifically for either Houses Kurita, Marik or the Federated Commonwealth found their way into the arsenals of all of them. During the Clan Invasion these manufacturers produced the new variants to meet the Clan threat while Vandenberg Industries continued to build original GRF-1N Griffins. When Vicore Industries began shopping around its "Project Phoenix" initiative, Defiance and Kallon Industries signed on to begin producing the completely redesigned GRF-6S Griffin. Victory Industries later signed up as well after the legal battle between Wolf's Dragoons and the Lyran Alliance saw the famous mercenary group selling its Light Fusion technology to both the Draconis Combine and Free Worlds League. The League designed a native update to the Griffin while ComStar had their own built as well which, ominously, soon began appearing in the ranks of the Word of Blake Militia. The Griffin would continue to remain a staple of the battlefields of the Inner Sphere during the maelstrom of the Jihad, the era of the Republic of the Sphere and the rise of the ilClan, with models still in production within the Free Worlds League and the Wolf Empire.
BMGriffin_GRF6SDAG10.deployment: The Lyran 6S Griffin was built in 3066 using an Earthwerks GRF Endo Steel chassis and mounted a Defiance 275 Light Fusion Engine for power. This allowed the 6S model to carry a Defiance 1001 ER PPC in the right arm, a Coventry StarFire LRM-15 over the right shoulder with Artemis IV, and two RAMTech 1500Z ER Medium Lasers, one in the center torso and one in the left arm. It carried twelve tons of Starshield A armor plating using layered sections at steeper angles, which allowed it to withstand more attacks than the 6CS, but only ten double heat sinks. Two tons of LRM reloads were mounted in the right torso and protected by CASE. Although still carrying the five Rawlings 55 jump jets and Neil 6000 communications system of the original model, the targeting-tracking system was updated to a RCA Instatrack Mk X and, perhaps most importantly, the cockpit was renovated for additional comfort and incorporate a Full-Head Ejection System.
BMGriffin_GRF6SDAG10.manufacturer: Defiance Industries,Victory Industries (formerly Norse BattleMech Works),Kallon Weapon Industries

BMOstscout_OTT9CSM.overview: The Ostscout was designed as a pure recon BattleMech by Ostmann Industries. To that end, it was built entirely around gathering data and getting out of trouble, tasks for which it is exceptional.
BMOstscout_OTT9CSM.capabilities: The Ostscout is quick enough to escape most traps, and very few other designs can match it in terms of speed and maneuverability. However its ability to run and leap out of danger came at the expense of offensive capability. In fact were it not for aggressive lobbying on the part of its test pilots the final production model would have been completely weaponless. As it is, the Ostscout would be hard-pressed to win a fight against all but the lightest 'Mechs. A poor combatant, the 'Mech excels at operating deep behind enemy lines, gathering as much information as possible about the terrain and the disposition of enemy forces. The true centerpiece of the design is its advanced sensor systems, including the TRSS.2L3 target-tracking system and powerful narrow-band Barret 4000 comm system. The sensor arrays themselves are mounted outside the main chassis due to their delicate nature, with the Ostscout using its arms to aim them. Everything from hydrological to geological data is recorded, so much data in fact that the 'Mech's computer cannot process it fast enough. This forces the Ostscout to move slowly when traveling through an area of interest, waving its arms seemingly at random, which makes it one of the few times the 'Mech is vulnerable to the enemy. However so long as the enemy's first salvo doesn't cripple it, the Ostscout will likely escape from an ambush.
BMOstscout_OTT9CSM.history: Starting in 2600 Ostmann built and sold the Ostscout to fulfill many armies' need for a swift reconnaissance 'Mech, but eventually found that demand was outstripping their production ability. Rather than sacrifice their popular Ostroc line of urban-combat 'Mechs, the company licensed Kong Interstellar to start building the 'Mech in 2700, an arrangement similar to that struck regarding the Ostsol. Kong would continue to build Ostscouts for the next hundred years until the destruction of their factory on Connaught at the outset of the Succession Wars. Deprived of the possibility of replacement, many commanders began to hoard their Ostscouts like valuable treasure, parceling them out only for special missions. Most Ostscout pilots would not even attempt to engage enemy 'Mechs, as the advanced sensor system became extremely rare and nearly impossible to replace. This unwillingness to put the 'Mech in danger meant many survived the Succession Wars in practically mint condition, although many which suffered damage to their advanced sensors were forced to replace them with inferior, albeit more robust, systems. Besides the Great Houses, ComStar also utilized the Ostscout, and in the aftermath of the Clan Invasion and ComStar Schism began developing a new Ostscout variant for their Com Guards. This new model would maintain the same maneuverability and intelligence-gathering capabilities of the original while improving its offensive and defensive capabilities. Debuting with success in 3064, within the next three years nearly half of all Com Guard Ostscouts had been upgraded to the new variant; however it was soon discovered that both the Lyran Alliance and Word of Blake were fielding their own updated Ostscouts identical to ComStar's. The intelligence leak would be confirmed and traced back to Dag Kesselring, former Precentor of the 66th Division, who passed on information about the program to both the Lyrans and Blakists. Used by both sides in the Blakist Jihad, the newborn Republic of the Sphere would maintain production of the 11J model Ostscout after the fall of Terra both for its own relatively limited needs as well as export sales to the Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth. Still produced during the Dark Age era, aside from the Krupp plant's combat focused Phoenix models both Kong Interstellar and Robinson Standard BattleWorks reintroduced variants that lean more heavily towards the original look and recon aspects of the venerable 7J model.
BMOstscout_OTT9CSM.deployment: The 9CS model is a complete upgrade of the venerable Ostscout, developed by ComStar and introduced in 3064. The 'Mech has been rebuilt from the ground up with a Krupp 255 Endo Steel internal structure. While still maintaining the same number of jump jets the design uses a 280 VOX extralight engine to free up weight for advanced electronics and weaponry. The arm-mounted sensor arrays were shifted to fixed points around the torso and included new side-scanning, Doppler and triangulation sensors to maintain the same data-gathering capability. Additionally a new high-speed computer, capable of handling terabytes of data in seconds, meant the Ostscout no longer had to slow down when using its sensors. The targeting-tracking system was also replaced with a TRSS Eagle Eye system mated to a Beagle Active Probe, Guardian ECM, and head-mounted TAG, while the comm system was upgraded to the Exeter Longscan 300 w/C3i Computer for better fire mission coordination. For self-defense, the 9CS model carries two Diverse Optics ER Medium Lasers in either arm and an Diverse Optics ER Small Laser in its center torso. Finally six tons of Krupp 155 Ferro-Fibrous armor provides superior protection from weapons fire.
BMOstscout_OTT9CSM.manufacturer: Kong Interstellar Corporation,Kong Interstellar Corporation,Ostmann Industries

BMOstsol_OTL6DCustom.overview:
The Ostsol emerged in 2694 as Ostmann Industries' answer to demands for an ammunition-independent heavy 'Mech capable of extended independent operations. Rather than compete with their own successful Ostroc line, Ostmann licensed the new design to Kong Interstellar Corporation, whose production facilities on Connaught could meet Star League Defense Force requirements. The first Ostsols entered service with SLDF Hussar and Dragoon regiments, where their all-energy armament proved ideal for deep raids and extended deployments.

The Ostsol's design philosophy prioritized self-sufficiency over raw firepower. Armed exclusively with lasers and requiring no ammunition resupply, the 'Mech could operate behind enemy lines indefinitely, limited only by its pilot's endurance. This capability, combined with sophisticated sensor systems and respectable speed, made the Ostsol a natural choice for reconnaissance lance command positions despite its heavy weight classification.
BMOstsol_OTL6DCustom.capabilities:
The Ostsol mounts two Tronel III Heavy large lasers in the side torsos as primary armament, delivering substantial damage at medium-to-long ranges. Four Tronel II medium lasers provide close-range firepower, with two mounted forward and two covering the rear arc. This rear-firing capability distinguishes the Ostsol from most heavy 'Mechs, allowing it to discourage pursuit and engage multiple opponents simultaneously, though it necessarily limits the firepower available against any single target.

The highly sensitive TRSS.2L3 targeting-tracking system represents one of the Ostsol's most valuable assets. Capable of detecting enemies at extended ranges even in difficult terrain, this electronics suite frequently led to Ostsols being assigned as lance command platforms despite the design's cavalry origins. Great care was invested in preserving these sensors during the technology-poor Succession Wars, as they could not be easily replaced.

A nineteen-ton Vlar 300 engine drives the Ostsol to 86 kilometers per hour, matching the Ostroc's speed while sixteen heat sinks manage the considerable thermal load of the all-laser armament. Nine tons of armor provide adequate protection, though like its sister design, the Ostsol suffers from weak rear armor that makes prolonged rear-arc engagements inadvisable despite the presence of rear-firing weapons. The 'Mech's fully functional hands make it particularly effective in physical combat, compensating somewhat for its inability to concentrate all weapons forward.
BMOstsol_OTL6DCustom.history:
Kong Interstellar's Ostsol production served the SLDF exclusively until 2752, when an amendment to Council Edict 2650 permitted sales to Member States. This wider distribution ensured the design's survival when Kong's Connaught facilities were destroyed during the First Succession War. Unable to manufacture complete 'Mechs, Kong continued producing spare parts that kept the widely-dispersed Ostsol fleet operational throughout the Succession Wars era.

The design's fortunes improved dramatically when Kong partnered with Free Worlds League engineers to produce the OTL-5M, incorporating recovered Star League technology just as the Clan Invasion began. This upgrade replaced the standard weapons with pulse laser variants and added an anti-missile system, though the use of an extralight engine made the refit controversial among traditionalists who valued the original's durability.

A second major revival occurred in 3064 when Duke James Sandoval's unsanctioned invasion of the Draconis Combine backfired catastrophically. With the FedCom Civil War consuming available military production, Robinson Standard BattleWorks received orders to identify older designs suitable for rapid modernization. The Ostsol proved an excellent candidate, and RSB's OTL-6D refit incorporated triple-strength myomer, advanced lasers sourced from the Outworlds Alliance, and a sophisticated targeting computer. These refits helped replenish Draconis March forces depleted by the failed invasion.

The Jihad saw Kong Interstellar's facilities damaged again during the liberation of Connaught, destroying their orbital endo steel production capability and XL engine stockpiles. Working with RAF specialist Rebecca O'Donaghue, Kong developed the OTL-9R as an assault-weight substitute using a standard engine and heavy-duty gyro. The Republic era brought further variants, and Clan Sea Fox's acquisition of Kong's design plans led to the Ostsol C, featuring Clan-grade weapons and reflective armor. Inner Sphere customers have eagerly purchased these advanced models despite their Clan origins.
BMOstsol_OTL6DCustom.deployment: Robinson Standard BattleWorks developed this variant in 3064 when Duke James Sandoval's ill-advised invasion of the Draconis Combine left the Draconis March desperately short of operational 'Mechs. With the FedCom Civil War consuming available production elsewhere, RSB received orders to modernize older designs for rapid deployment. Kong Interstellar provided technical schematics for the Ostsol, having performed factory refits for years. The resulting variant incorporated triple-strength myomer that provided devastating physical combat capability when running hot, an extralight engine, and ferro-fibrous armor that significantly altered the 'Mech's appearance. Advanced lasers sourced from Lushann Industries in the Outworlds Alliance (part of that nation's "Long Road" reform program) proved so reliable they were later used on the Black Knight BL-12-KNT and Sagittaire SGT-8R. Draconis March Militia and Robinson Rangers received most examples.

CVGoblinInfantrySupportVehicle_Custom.overview:
The Goblin Infantry Support Vehicle is Johnston Industries' comprehensive redesign of the Goblin for the Clan Invasion era. Federated Commonwealth commanders facing power-armored Elemental infantry for the first time found the original Goblin's large laser and conventional infantry bay dangerously inadequate. Johnston redesigned the vehicle from the ground up, replacing the aging ICE powerplant with a fusion engine, upgrading the weapons suite for anti-battle-armor work, and expanding the infantry bay to carry a full platoon.

The result, entering production in 3053, redefined the Goblin from a medium tank with infantry capacity to a dedicated infantry fighting vehicle. Johnston classified it separately from its predecessor, reflecting the depth of the redesign and the shift in intended role.
CVGoblinInfantrySupportVehicle_Custom.capabilities:
The Goblin ISV's weapons suite is purpose-built for combined-arms close-range combat. The Sutel Precision Line large pulse laser forms the primary weapon, combining pulse accuracy with energy weapon endurance, and is especially effective against power-armored targets. The Harpoon-6 SRM 6 adds short-range punch capable of threatening BattleMechs and heavy vehicles, while two Johnston Miniguns handle conventional infantry. The MainFire Point-Defense anti-missile system increases survivability against missile-heavy opponents, though its limited ammunition restricts its effectiveness to the first several volleys of an engagement.

The Fireheart 180 fusion engine enables expansion of the infantry bay to full platoon capacity. Nearly ten tons of Durallex Light ferro-fibrous armor make the Goblin ISV among the most heavily protected vehicles of its weight class, a significant upgrade from the original Goblin's standard protection.

The design's primary weakness is its lack of long-range firepower. Commanders must pair Goblin ISVs with indirect fire assets to shape engagements before the vehicle can close effectively. The vehicle's modest speed also makes it dependent on other units to control terrain in advance of its approach, and experienced opponents learn to force engagements beyond short range where the ISV cannot contribute fully.
CVGoblinInfantrySupportVehicle_Custom.history:
Johnston Industries began redesigning the Goblin shortly after the initial Clan advance, responding to urgent requests from AFFC commanders who had encountered Elemental battle armor for the first time. The new design replaced the aging ICE powerplant with a Fireheart 180 fusion engine, enabling expansion of the infantry bay to full platoon capacity, and replaced the large laser with a pulse laser system and SRM rack better suited to anti-battle-armor work. Production of the Goblin ISV began in 3053, with some prototypes seeing action during the final months of the initial Clan Invasion.

The Goblin ISV's first major operational test came in 3057 on Hsien in the Sarna March. After Marik forces destroyed the Second Federated Commonwealth RCT's aerospace assets, McCarron's Armored Cavalry dropped onto the planet and assaulted the RCT's ground forces. The Second FedCom RCT's commander committed the Goblin ISV battalion to the battle for Chengde, where close-quarters urban fighting played to the vehicle's strengths. The Goblins inflicted significant losses on the Capellan mercenary forces before attrition reduced the battalion to only seven operational vehicles. The engagement demonstrated both the ISV's combat effectiveness in urban terrain and its vulnerability in sustained attritional fighting without adequate resupply.

During the FedCom Civil War, Goblin ISVs fought in virtually every major engagement, serving as the backbone of conventional regiments from Federated Suns forces. Heavy urban fighting on Tikograd and New Moskau on Tikonov demonstrated the ISV's suitability for close-quarters combined-arms operations. The battle for New Syrtis brought Goblin ISVs into particularly desperate action, with vehicles rolling directly from Johnston Industries' assembly lines into defensive positions around the capital.

The Jihad era tested the New Syrtis facility severely. A Capellan counterattack was repelled through the efforts of the Fourth Donegal Guards and Johnston's own security forces, but subsequent Taurian strikes contaminated the production site with radiation. The government declared the facility too hazardous for workers, halting production at the primary line and forcing Johnston to shift manufacturing to its Benet III component factory to maintain continuity. Cleanup efforts continued into the early 3080s. The Goblin ISV nonetheless remained a common vehicle in Federated Suns service throughout this period, with surviving units continuing to operate and field-modified examples supplementing production shortfalls.
CVGoblinInfantrySupportVehicle_Custom.deployment: The Goblin ISV serves as a primary IFV throughout Federated Suns mechanized infantry formations. It is particularly common in the Ceti Hussar regiments and other AFFS units with strong conventional infantry components. The vehicle is most effective in urban and close terrain, where its short-range weapons profile and platoon-capacity infantry bay enable combined-arms operations. Commanders routinely attach Goblin ISV platoons to infantry-heavy task forces and assault formations expecting close-quarters fighting.

CVManticoreHeavyTank_Custom.overview: The Manticore is one of the most widely produced and respected heavy tanks in the Inner Sphere, originally designed by TechniCorp as an infantry support vehicle capable of engaging BattleMechs on favorable terms. Introduced during the Reunification War in 2575, the sixty-ton tracked vehicle was built to fill the gap between lighter screening vehicles and the massive assault tanks that dominated battlefield formations. Its combination of long-range fire support, close-range punch, and respectable armor protection made it an attractive option for military planners across the Star League. After TechniCorp's destruction during the Amaris Coup, the design's production licenses spread to manufacturers across the Inner Sphere and beyond. The Manticore remains in frontline service with nearly every major military power, a remarkable achievement for a design approaching five centuries of continuous production.
CVManticoreHeavyTank_Custom.capabilities:
The Manticore's primary weapon is the Parti-Kill Heavy Cannon particle projection cannon, which uses magnetic collection bottles to charge plasma that loses cohesion and disintegrates targets at ranges approaching 540 meters. A FarFire LRM-10 rack mounted on independent swivel mounts above the turret provides supplementary long-range fire with a full 120-degree arc independent of the main turret. At closer ranges, the SureShot Mk VI SRM-6 launcher and hull-mounted OMI HighBurn medium laser round out the weapon array, giving the Manticore credible firepower at every engagement distance.

The Pitban 240 fusion engine gives the tank a respectable cruise speed of 43 km/h and a top speed of 65 km/h, a significant advantage over vehicles reliant on internal combustion engines during the Succession Wars when fuel supplies were unreliable. Eleven tons of ArcShield Maxi II armor provide solid protection for a vehicle of its tonnage. The Manticore's chief weakness is that it lacks the concentrated firepower of heavier vehicles such as the Behemoth and Demolisher, making it a poor choice for head-on engagements with assault-class opponents. Manticore crews are trained to avoid such confrontations, leveraging their mobility and range to control engagements on their own terms.
CVManticoreHeavyTank_Custom.history:
TechniCorp developed the Manticore during the Reunification War for the Star League member states, creating an infantry support weapon that could hold its own against BattleMechs in the right circumstances. The design proved so successful that production continued uninterrupted through the Star League era, with TechniCorp's Terra-based headquarters overseeing a network of licensed manufacturers across the Inner Sphere.

The Amaris Coup proved catastrophic for TechniCorp. When Stefan Amaris seized Terra, TechniCorp's head offices were destroyed along with their primary production facility. Rather than ending the Manticore's story, this event scattered the design across the Inner Sphere as surviving subsidiary manufacturers absorbed the production technology. Defiance Industries on Hesperus II, Jalastar Aerospace on Panpour, Quikscell Company on Ares, and several other firms continued building the tank independently.

The Succession Wars tested the Manticore's design philosophy. While most combat vehicles relied on internal combustion engines that were cheaper and easier to maintain, the Manticore's fusion engine demanded more resources. This made each tank expensive to produce and difficult to repair, but the fusion engine's reliability and the elimination of fuel logistics concerns proved invaluable during prolonged campaigns. Commanders who could afford Manticores found them worth every C-bill, and the tank's popularity endured even as lighter and cheaper alternatives flooded the battlefield.

Licensing the vehicle to companies across multiple states spread the Manticore's reputation to the farthest corners of the Inner Sphere and parts of the Periphery. Defiance Industries drew criticism when it started Manticore production on Proserpina through its relationship with Bulldog Enterprises, effectively arming the Draconis Combine. Defiance defended the decision by arguing that the Combine's weapons manufacturer, Bulldog Enterprises, was already attempting to clone the vehicle for House Kurita. It was better for the Commonwealth to control the licensing and profit from the arrangement.

The technological renaissance of the 3050s brought significant changes to the Manticore family. Defiance Industries developed the 3055 Upgrade, replacing the original particle cannon with a large pulse laser and adding ferro-fibrous armor while retaining the basic chassis and engine to allow easy field conversion of existing vehicles. The upgrade's focus on improved accuracy through fire-control systems rather than raw firepower reflected the changing nature of combined-arms warfare. Both Allied and Loyalist forces fielded the upgraded design during the FedCom Civil War, and many upgrade kits were imported into the Federated Commonwealth.

Bulldog Industries on Proserpina introduced C3-equipped variants in 3063, integrating the Combine's networking technology into the Manticore chassis. The New Earth Trading Company developed the LB-X variant using unproduced Defiance plans, mounting an autocannon effective against battle armor during the Civil War. Jalastar Aerospace followed with an experimental rotary autocannon variant in 3069, and Bulldog developed the Heavy PPC variant during the Jihad in 3074, selling the schematics to Quikscell and Jalastar to broaden production.

The Manticore's enduring popularity led Defiance Industries to develop the Manticore II in 3112, a heavier seventy-ton design optimized for amphibious operations. Drawing on that design's principles, Defiance then licensed the Manticore XL back to the original production network in 3117. This lighter variant incorporated an extra-light engine and a targeting computer, updating the classic chassis for modern warfare while maintaining the broad manufacturing base that had sustained the Manticore for centuries. In the Magistracy of Canopus, Majesty Metals and Manufacturing maintained continuous Manticore production from the Star League through the ilClan period, an unbroken run that few other factories could claim.
CVManticoreHeavyTank_Custom.deployment: The base Manticore remains in service with military forces across the Inner Sphere and beyond, fielded by every Great House and numerous Periphery states. Its long production history and widespread manufacturing base make replacement parts readily available, ensuring the design's continued viability even in less industrialized regions. Many wealthy nobles who cannot afford a full BattleMech formation will field companies of Manticores instead.
